pending_interview.category: Martech/AI-product — personalization architecture, attribution modeling, GenAI content pipelines, measurement under privacy constraints
pending_interview.question: A B2B software company has a marketing team that runs email campaigns, paid ads, and a content hub. They want to use AI to personalize content recommendations on their content hub and attribute pipeline influence — meaning, understand which pieces of content actually moved a prospect closer to buying — across a buying cycle that often takes six to nine months. Their CRM (customer relationship management system — the database that tracks leads and customers) has good deal-stage data but spotty engagement data, and third-party cookies (small tracking files that let advertisers follow users across websites — these are being phased out by browsers) are no longer reliably available. How would you design a measurement and personalization architecture for this team, what data foundations would you prioritize building first, and what are the biggest risks to getting this wrong?
